display.purpose: The single page headline. One per page, always exactly two non-wrapping lines, sized to clear the right-hand illustration.

title.purpose: Card and component titles, and the card's first-movement figure.

body.purpose: Running text and every form control — 1rem keeps iOS from force-zooming a focused field.

figure.purpose: Big numbers and the three-letter service tags — display weight as a graphic mark.

lead.purpose: The paragraph directly under a headline, capped at 46ch. Never name a colour `lead` again.

body-md.purpose: Denser supporting tier: card copy, contact promises, confirmations.

body-sm.purpose: Footer links and the brand line under the wordmark.

label-sm.purpose: Captions, metadata, field labels, bullet lists, the origin stamp.

wordmark.purpose: Fixed lockup size. Not a reading step — it never rescales with the document.

shadows.name: hard-offset
shadows.purpose: Primary button hover only. Zero blur, zero spread — a printed graphic offset, not simulated light. The system's only shadow.

motion.name: ease-enter
motion.purpose: Opening, expanding and revealing. Drawer open (260ms) and the disclosure indicator (250ms).

motion.name: ease-exit
motion.purpose: Closing and collapsing. Drawer close (210ms) — faster out than in.

motion.name: dur-press
motion.purpose: Button transform on hover. Fast enough to feel mechanical.

motion.name: dur-state
motion.purpose: Color, background and border-color state changes across all controls.

motion.name: dur-reveal
motion.purpose: Atmospheric opacity fades in the hero canvas layer.

motion.name: fps-idle
motion.purpose: Ambient canvas drift is capped at 30fps and disabled entirely without a fine pointer.

motion.name: hold-between-passes
motion.purpose: Stillness after each pass of the shortlist field. Back to back the passes read as a mechanism idling; separated, each reads as an event.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The go signal. Chartreuse fill, square corners, lifts into a hard offset shadow on hover.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action. A ghost becomes a primary on hover rather than merely brightening.

components.name: Service Card
components.description: The primary content object. Whole surface is the click target; text brightens with the surface so the card responds as one thing.

components.name: Disclosure Toggle
components.description: Signature component. Reads as a control, not a link — fills solid chartreuse on hover or keyboard focus. The plus indicator loses its vertical stroke when open.

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Ink fill, 2px field-line border, square corners. Set at 1rem so iOS does not force-zoom on focus.

components.name: Select Field
components.description: Native appearance stripped and replaced with an inline chartreuse triangle so selects match text inputs exactly.

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: Condensed tracked capitals, dim at rest, chartreuse on hover. Right-justified against the primary button.

narrative.overview:
This system borrows the visual language of worksite signage: the hi-vis vest, the hazard placard, the equipment tag bolted to a skid. Everything is built to be read at a glance, in bad light, by someone who is busy and not inclined to be sold to. That constraint produces the whole aesthetic — maximum contrast, heavy condensed capitals, flat opaque surfaces, no ornament that does not carry information.

The audience is Alberta oilfield and energy operators. They are surrounded by this language every day, so it reads as native rather than as a theme. The system earns credibility the way the copy does: by being fluent rather than by claiming fluency. A softer, more conventional agency look would read as an outsider's guess at the industry; this reads like it came from inside it.

Density is deliberately uneven. Headline type is enormous and crowds the viewport; supporting text is small, tight and workmanlike. The gap between those two scales is the drama in the system — there is almost nothing in the middle. The logo is a fixed inherited asset and the palette carries green to match it, which is why the darkest neutrals are green-biased rather than true black.
keyCharacteristics: Hi-vis chartreuse against near-black, with hazard orange as a second signal
Zero corner radius anywhere in the system
Heavy condensed display capitals against small tracked condensed labels
Flat surfaces at rest; depth appears only as a response to interaction
Structural borders at 3px, control borders at 2px — borders do the work shadows usually do

rules.name: The Ten Percent Rule
rules.body: No viewport is more than roughly ten percent Safety Chartreuse. Its authority comes entirely from its rarity; a page that is 30% chartreuse has no accent at all, only noise. Audit test: squint at any screen — if more than one element shouts, cut until one does.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: Chartreuse means go, press, this is live. Orange means look out, this is the problem. The two never swap jobs and orange never appears on a call to action. Orange may be used generously in graphic and editorial roles; it may never be used to invite a click.

rules.name: The Green Ground Rule
rules.body: Neutrals are biased green, never neutral grey and never true black. The logo is fixed and inherited; the palette bends toward it so the mark never looks pasted on.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Type is either very large or very small; the middle is almost empty. A headline and its label can sit inches apart in scale and still feel like one system. Resist introducing intermediate sizes to bridge them — the gap is the design.

rules.name: The Tracked Capitals Rule
rules.body: All uppercase text is condensed and tracked to at least 0.10em, and 0.13–0.24em for anything under 0.8rem. Untracked small capitals are illegible and instantly read as an error. Running body copy is never uppercase.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Shadows are a response to interaction, never a property of a surface. If an element is not being touched, it is flat. Any blurred or ambient shadow is outside this system.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: No radius. Not on buttons, not on tags, not on images, not just a little on inputs. The square corner is load-bearing identity; one rounded element makes the whole page look like a different template.

rules.name: The Honest Affordance Rule
rules.body: If a surface changes on hover, that whole surface must be clickable. A tile that highlights but does nothing is a broken promise — either make the whole thing the control or remove the hover state. Corollary: no interaction may be hover-only; every hover behavior needs a tap or click equivalent.

rules.name: The One Namespace Rule
rules.body: A colour and a type step may never share a name. Tailwind's text-* utility serves both --color-* and --text-*, so a colour token named `lead` silently shadowed the `lead` type step and the Lead size never rendered. Audit test: for every --text-<name>, confirm no --color-<name> exists.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: A font-size literal in component markup is a defect, not a shortcut. Needed twice, it becomes a named step in @theme; needed once, it snaps to the nearest existing step.

rules.name: The Own Ground Rule
rules.body: Text never sits on generated artwork and hopes. Either it carries its own opaque ground, or the layout moves it off the artwork entirely. Contrast that depends on where a mark happened to land is not contrast.

rules.name: The Coupled Motion Rule
rules.body: When two elements exchange places, their motions must share one easing window. Independent continuous motions in the same frame read as unrelated activity, however well each one is tuned individually.

dos: Do keep Safety Chartreuse under roughly 10% of any viewport (The Ten Percent Rule).
Do use the two border tiers meaningfully — 3px for objects, 2px for controls.
Do set every piece of small type in Barlow Condensed, uppercase, tracked to at least 0.10em.
Do let full-bleed color bands carry section rhythm instead of horizontal rules.
Do brighten a component's text along with its surface on hover, so the object responds as a whole.
Do fade atmospheric graphics out with a mask so they dissolve into the ground.
Do give every hover behavior a click or tap equivalent.
Do resolve every font-size to a named step; promote a size to @theme when it is needed twice, snap it to the nearest step when it is needed once (The One Ramp Rule).
Do set form controls at a full 1rem so iOS does not force-zoom a focused field.
Do give any label sitting over the atmospheric field its own opaque ground.
Do declare each section's data-ground so the separator rule can tell a colour change from a spacing boundary.
Do separate repeated passes of an ambient animation with a hold; continuous repetition reads as a mechanism rather than an event.
donts: Don't introduce any border-radius, at any size, anywhere (The Square Corner Rule).
Don't use blurred, ambient, or resting shadows. The only shadow is a hard 4px offset on button hover.
Don't put Hazard Orange on a call to action — it is the warning signal, not the go signal (The Two Signals Rule).
Don't use neutral grey or true black. Neutrals are green-biased so the fixed logo belongs.
Don't frame a full-bleed atmospheric canvas in a hard-edged box — a visible rectangle around ambient artwork was explicitly rejected; mask and fade it instead.
Don't build simulated product UI — mock dashboards, fake chat transcripts, fake result panels — to illustrate a claim. This was explicitly rejected as cluttered and artificial.
Don't bookend the page with full-width diagonal stripe bands; that treatment was tried and rejected.
Don't add intermediate type sizes to soften the jump between display and label. The scale gap is intentional.
Don't name a colour token and a type step the same word — Tailwind's text-* utility serves both namespaces and the colour silently wins (The One Namespace Rule).
Don't unmount a form to show an error. The inputs are uncontrolled; replacing them throws away everything the visitor typed.
Don't double the section separator by padding both neighbours on a shared ground.
Don't recompute shadowBlur, or any blur, inside an animation frame.
Don't animate an exchange as two independent loops; couple the mover and the moved to one easing window.
